title: package.xi
concept: package.xi is the project manifest defining metadata, dependencies, and build configuration
why: A project is more than source code — it has a name, version, authors, dependencies, and build settings. `package.xi` centralizes this metadata so tools (xiom CLI, IDEs, CI/CD) can understand the project structure without parsing every source file. It's the entry point that makes a directory a XIOM project.
theory: `package.xi` is a declarative file at the root of every XIOM project. It specifies: package identity (`name`, `version`), build target (`binary` or `library`), compiler settings (`edition`, `optimization`), and dependency declarations. The file is parsed before compilation begins and drives the compiler's resolution strategy. XIOM's manifest format is a custom key-value syntax — more structured than TOML, less verbose than JSON, designed for humans to write.
code_template:
package calculator
  version: "0.1.0"
  target: binary
  edition: "2025"

dependencies:
  math_utils: "^1.2"

# Source files are automatically discovered from src/
solution:
package axiom_engine
  version: "0.2.0"
  target: library
  edition: "2025"
  authors: ["XIOM Team <team@axiom.dev>"]
  description: "A lightweight game engine for XIOM"

dependencies:
  vulkan_bindings: "^0.9"
  glfw_windowing: "^1.0"

# Library exports are defined in src/lib.xi
tips: Always pin major versions in dependencies to avoid breakage
Set `target: library` for reusable crates, `binary` for executables
Run `xiom pkg verify` to check manifest validity
common_mistakes: Forgetting to update version before publishing
Missing `target` field — compiler won't know what to build
Incorrect semver format causing parse errors
